::: {#exr-chebyshev-sample-size}

#### How many cars to estimate mean fuel economy

Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ be [IID](independence.qmd#def-iid) draws of the fuel economy (`mpg`) of
a car chosen at random from the Auto data,
with population mean $\mean$ and variance $\varpar$,
and let $\samplemean{X}{n} \eqdef \avgin X_i$.

a.  Use @thm-sum-iid-moments and @thm-chebyshev to show that for every $\epsilon > 0$,

    $$
    \Prf{\abs{\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean} \ge \epsilon} \le \frac{\varpar}{n\epsilon^2}
    $$

b.  Compute $\varpar$ for the `mpg` column of
    [`data/auto.csv`](data/auto.csv),
    treating the 392 cars as the whole population.
    Find the smallest $n$ for which the bound in (a) guarantees
    $\Prf{\abs{\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean} \ge 1} \le 0.05$.

c.  Simulate 10,000 samples of that size drawn with replacement,
    and count how many sample means miss $\mean$ by 1 or more.
    Why is the count so far below the 5% the bound allows?

:::
